fixes.d: The Senate Community Affairs References Committee tabled 'Forgotten Australians: A report on Australians who experienced institutional or out-of-home care as children' on 30 August 2004. It received 614 submissions and estimated that about 500,000 people had been placed in institutions or foster care, and heard accounts of neglect, beatings, psychological cruelty, forced labour and sexual assault and rape by carers, other children, visitors and foster families. Prime Minister Kevin Rudd apologised in Parliament to Forgotten Australians and former child migrants on 16 November 2009.

note: Replaced the Wikipedia url with the Senate committee's tabling speeches page (30 August 2004, 614 submissions, about 500,000 placed in care, sexual assault and rape among abuses); Wikipedia confirms the 2009 Rudd apology. Replaced 'hundreds of accounts' with the 614-submission figure.

fixes.d: Colombia's Commission for the Clarification of Truth published its volume on children and adolescents, 'No es un mal menor', in July 2022. It documented 16,238 children recruited by armed groups between 1990 and 2017 and estimated the real number at 27,101 to 40,828, and described recruitment as intentional and systematic, including use of minors by the state security forces. It found that recruited girls were forced to use contraception at an early age, forced to have abortions, and subjected to harassment, rape and sexual torture.

note: Checked the Truth Commission chapter PDF: 16,238 recruited 1990-2017, estimate 27,101-40,828, forced contraception, forced abortions, harassment, rape and sexual torture of recruited girls, and a chapter on use of minors by the state security forces; UNICEF page has 'intencional y sistemático'. The claim that boys suffered these abuses less often was not found, so removed it.

It identified 61 accused clergy and at least 121 known victims. fixes.d: An investigation ordered by the Danish government in 2020, financed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Elderly and carried out by Danmarks Forsorgsmuseum (Svendborg Museum), was published in March 2022. It documented widespread abuse and neglect, including sexual assault, of children, young people and adults placed in state special-care institutions between 1933 and 1980, and found the state did not carry out systematic oversight. About 15,000 people with disabilities were committed. Social affairs minister Pernille Rosenkrantz-Theil gave an official apology on behalf of the state at Horsens on 11 September 2023.

note: Checked The Local and the SDU page: ordered in 2020, financed by the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Elderly, carried out by Danmarks Forsorgsmuseum (Svendborg Museum), published March 2022, 1933-1980, about 15,000 people, sexual assault documented. The apology at Horsens on 11 September 2023 was given by social affairs minister Pernille Rosenkrantz-Theil, not Mette Frederiksen; corrected. Sources do not separate sexual abuse of children from abuse of adults.

The press kit attributes the omerta phrase to the commission itself, not to inspectorate inquiries; reworded cover.

fixes.d: The Child Exploitation and Online Protection Centre announced in January 2011 a thematic assessment of 'localised grooming' and published 'Out of mind, out of sight' later that year. It recorded 2,379 offenders since the start of 2008, mostly men aged 18 to 24 (38% white, 26% Asian, 3% black, ethnicity unknown in 32%), with about 90% of victims white. It found about two-thirds of Local Safeguarding Children Boards were not meeting national guidance and that victims did not expect to be believed. CEOP warned the data were not comprehensive enough to draw firm conclusions.

note: Checked Yorkshire Post and BASW: the 2,379 figure is offenders, not cases; ethnicity was unknown in 32% (not 'where known'); about 90% of victims white; two in three LSCBs not meeting guidance; victims did not expect to be believed; CEOP said data incomplete. Corrected d.

fixes.d: Childcare worker Robert Mikelsons abused babies and toddlers at two Amsterdam daycare centres and as a babysitter between February 2007 and January 2010. On 21 May 2012 the Amsterdam district court sentenced him to 18 years plus compulsory psychiatric detention (TBS); he was charged over 67 children and admitted abusing 87, and the appeal court raised the sentence to 19 years on 26 April 2013. His partner Richard van O. was sentenced to six years as an accessory. On 15 April 2011 a commission chaired by Louise Gunning-Schepers found that daycare centres, government bodies and others had failed, that risk signals were missed, and that a 2008 anonymous report had not been acted on.

note: Checked DutchNews (21 May 2012: 18 years plus psychiatric detention, charged over 67, admitted 87, February 2007 to January 2010) and AT5 (Gunning commission 15 April 2011, failures, missed signals, 2008 Meld Misdaad Anoniem tip a missed opportunity); Wikipedia gives the 26 April 2013 appeal to 19 years. Clarified that Richard van O. got six years as an accessory (he was acquitted of separate possession and assault charges).

fixes.d: Nepal's National Human Rights Commission, through its Office of the Special Rapporteur on Trafficking in Persons, has published national reports on trafficking since 2005. Its report released in August 2019 estimated that about 35,000 Nepalis were trafficked in 2018, including 5,000 children, and that nearly 1.5 million were at risk. It said nearly 1,000 Nepali women and girls are rescued from India each year and that poor screening at the open border makes cross-border trafficking hard to control. Its 2018 report said girls and women are trafficked to India for prostitution, orchestra dancing, circus work and marriage, and some are moved on to third countries.

note: Checked Kathmandu Post (6 Aug 2019) and the NHRC 2017-18 report. The NHRC series runs since 2005, not 2012-13; the 35,000 (15,000 men, 15,000 women, 5,000 children) is for 2018, so y0 set to 2018. The Post does not give the purposes of trafficking to India; replaced with the NHRC report's wording (prostitution, orchestra dancing, circus, marriage, onward to third countries). The 5,000 children include labour trafficking.

fixes.d: Paraguay's Comisión de Verdad y Justicia, created by law in October 2003, presented its final report on 28 August 2008 after collecting more than 2,000 testimonies on the 1954–1989 dictatorship. Its conclusions state that sexual violence against women and girls was fostered by the repressive apparatus and reached its extreme in 'sexual slavery of girls practised by senior officers of the regime', and that young children were exploited economically and sexually in military posts at the service of officers. It recorded that 10.8% of victims were minors at the time and noted large under-reporting of sexual violence. Amnesty International reported that girls as young as seven were believed to have been taken from their homes for senior military officers.

note: Checked the final report PDF (28 Aug 2008; 'esclavitud sexual de niñas practicada por oficiales de nivel superior del régimen'; exploitation of young children in military posts; 10.8% minors; 2,059 testimonies; under-reporting) and Amnesty (law of 6 October 2003; girls as young as seven). The 'as young as seven' detail is Amnesty's, not the report's; reattributed.

fixes.who: Student houses in Karaman linked to the Ensar Foundation; student dormitories nationally
fixes.victims_note: a teacher in Karaman was arrested for abusing 10 children (Diken)
fixes.d: On 24 March 2016 the Turkish Grand National Assembly unanimously set up a research commission on child abuse after a teacher in Karaman was arrested for abusing 10 children in student houses, two of them owned by the Ensar Foundation. It began work on 28 April; by July its only field visit had been to Karaman, where the provincial family directorate gave members a report that blamed the victims' families. Its draft report in October 2016 recommended that the Education Ministry license and inspect student dormitories, a permanent children's rights committee in parliament, a child-protection coordination centre, background checks for people working with children and a wider penal definition of sexual abuse. Opposition (CHP) members said the report was general and theoretical and that the commission had not visited state nurseries, prisons or Syrian camps.

note: Checked Diken (24 March and 8 July 2016), BirGün (15 June and 13 Oct 2016) and bianet (2 Nov 2016). Unanimous setup 24 March, work from 28 April, only field trip by July was Karaman, provincial family directorate report blamed families, and the October draft recommendations are confirmed. KAİMDER and the claim that CHP said the report did not name administrators were not found; bianet says it later visited two Ankara institutions. Rewrote d and who; added victims 10 from Diken.

fixes.d: A report by special master Bob Troyer, a former US Attorney appointed by Attorney General Phil Weiser, was released on 23 October 2019. It found that 43 priests sexually abused at least 166 children in Colorado's three Catholic dioceses over about 70 years, the most recent reported case in 1998. On average it took 19.5 years from a credible allegation to a restriction on the priest, and more than half the victims were abused after the church already knew of the priest. A supplemental report followed on 1 December 2020.

note: Checked Colorado Public Radio (23 Oct 2019): 43 priests, 166 children, about 70 years, 19.5-year average delay, over half abused after the diocese knew, Troyer and Weiser, euphemisms, most recent abuse 1998; search results confirm the 1 December 2020 supplemental report. 'Most in the 1960s and 1970s' was not in the source, so removed.

Checked GAO product page (released 16 Dec 2010, 15 cases in 11 states) and the House committee release (at least 11 previously targeted children, at least 6 abused more after hiring, resignations, positive references, missing fingerprint checks, no federal law). Neither source gives the 2000-2010 range, so y0 and y1 removed.

fixes.victims_note: Investigators spoke with nearly 140 victims, witnesses and suspects in 15 states
fixes.d: A four-year Kansas Bureau of Investigation inquiry, requested by Archbishop Joseph Naumann and reported in January 2023, reviewed five decades of church records and identified 188 clergy suspected of crimes such as rape and sexual misconduct with children. Investigators spoke with nearly 140 victims, witnesses and suspects in 15 states and referred 30 cases to prosecutors, all of which were too old to charge. The KBI found the church had protected these men for decades, often by moving them to other parishes.

note: Checked WFAE (Kansas News Service, 15 Jan 2023): four-year probe, five decades, 188 clergy, 30 referrals all too old, moving priests, NDAs. The source says crimes 'such as rape and sexual misconduct with children' and that the nearly 140 interviewed were victims, witnesses and suspects; corrected d and victims_note.

No changes.
